MTX_FREQUENCY.title: Low-dose methotrexate dosing
MTX_FREQUENCY.summary: For rheumatoid arthritis and similar inflammatory diseases, low-dose methotrexate is generally administered once weekly, not once daily.
MTX_FREQUENCY.verification: Verify the indication, prescribed dose, route, and frequency against the current licensed clinical reference and hospital protocol.

MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.title: Methotrexate — patient-specific dosing
MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.summary: Methotrexate dosing is indication-specific and requires verification of the indication, dose, frequency, route, renal function, and other patient factors.
MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.verification: Check the current licensed clinical reference and hospital-approved protocol before accepting an unusual methotrexate order.

GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.title: Insulin glargine — basal insulin administration
GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.summary: Insulin glargine is a long-acting basal insulin generally administered once daily. An order for multiple daily administrations should be verified.
GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.verification: Confirm the insulin product, prescribed frequency, indication, and patient-specific factors using the current licensed reference and hospital protocol.

HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.title: Medication order numeric-entry safety
HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.summary: Unusual numerical dose entries may represent a prescribing or order-entry error and should be independently verified, particularly for high-alert medications.
HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.verification: Verify the intended dose with the prescriber and compare against the applicable hospital protocol and current clinical reference.

DOSE_FORMAT.title: Error-prone dose expressions
DOSE_FORMAT.summary: Dose expressions involving unsafe decimal formatting, missing leading zeros, or unnecessary trailing zeros can contribute to medication errors.
DOSE_FORMAT.verification: Review the dose expression and correct unsafe formatting according to institutional medication-safety standards.

ROUTE_MISMATCH.title: Route and dosage-form consistency
ROUTE_MISMATCH.summary: The prescribed route should be consistent with the medication, dosage form, indication, and available formulation.
ROUTE_MISMATCH.verification: Verify the intended route against the current licensed drug reference and hospital-approved formulary or protocol.

FREQUENCY_MISMATCH.title: Frequency and indication consistency
FREQUENCY_MISMATCH.summary: Medication frequency should be appropriate for the drug, indication, formulation, and patient-specific factors.
FREQUENCY_MISMATCH.verification: Verify the frequency using the current licensed clinical reference and applicable hospital protocol.
